summary: Defines an IKEv2 extension that lets an IKEv2 security association be created and authenticated without creating a Child SA. It is experimental and an independent submission, not an Internet Standards Track specification.

eli5.summary: Usually two computers set up their private chat line and the first conversation together. This lets them just prove who they are first and leave the conversation setup for later.

questions: create ikev2 sa without child sa
how to create an ikev2 sa without a child sa
why use ikev2 only for authentication
subtitle: An IKEv2 extension that sets up and authenticates a security association without also creating a Child SA.

tldr.problem: IKEv2 requires the IKE_AUTH exchange to try to create a Child SA along with the IKEv2 SA, which is inconvenient when a peer only wants authentication or has no traffic to protect yet.
tldr.mechanism: The responder advertises a CHILDLESS_IKEV2_SUPPORTED notification in its IKE_SA_INIT response. If it is present, the initiator may send a modified IKE_AUTH request that leaves out the Child SA parts.
tldr.outcome: Peers can hold an authenticated IKEv2 SA with no Child SA. This is an Experimental, independent-stream document, not a standard.

today: RFC 6023 is an Experimental, independent-stream RFC, and the RFC Editor makes no statement about its value for implementation or deployment. It builds on the IKEv2 specification in RFC 5996.

sections.title: Why a SA Without a Child SA
sections.content:
IKEv2, as specified in RFC 5996, requires that the IKE_AUTH exchange try to create a Child SA along with the IKEv2 SA. Some implementations only need IKEv2 for authentication, and others want to set up the IKEv2 SA before there is any traffic to protect.

The RFC argues that an IKEv2 SA without a Child SA is still useful. It allows liveness checks of the peer, quick setup of Child SAs later without public key operations or user interaction, authentication of the peer, and detection of NAT boxes between two hosts.
sections.eli5: It is like showing your ID at the door first and ordering food later. Showing your ID is useful even if you have not ordered anything yet.

sections.title: Usage Scenarios
sections.content:
The RFC lists several scenarios that motivated the extension:

  • Interactive remote access VPN, where the user says "connect" but there is no traffic yet, so the gateway cannot know which selectors to use.
  • Location-aware security, where all traffic is encrypted on an untrusted network but only the IKEv2 SA needs to be kept on a trusted one.
  • IKEv2 SAs kept only for liveness checks and for reporting the status of VPN links.
  • Physically secure links, such as Passive Optical Network links, where authentication is needed but traffic protection is not.
  • Use of IKEv2 for user authentication in RFC 5106.
  • Sending an INVALID_SPI notification in a protected INFORMATIONAL exchange.
  • A possible future extension that uses IKEv2 SAs to generate keying material for applications.

In some of these cases a dummy Child SA could be created and then removed, but the RFC says this causes undesirable side effects and race conditions. The peer might also treat the deletion of the Child SA as a reason to delete the IKEv2 SA.
sections.eli5: Sometimes you only need to know your friend is really who they say, or that they are still there. You do not need to start a game yet.

sections.title: How Support Is Negotiated
sections.content:
The responder decides whether to allow an IKE_AUTH exchange without a piggy-backed Child SA negotiation. A supporting responder MUST include the notification in its IKE_SA_INIT response.

An initiator MAY send the modified IKE_AUTH request only if it saw that notification, and MUST NOT send it otherwise. A responder that advertised support MUST process the modified request and reply with a modified response, and MUST NOT send a modified response if the initiator did not send a modified request.

A responder configured not to support the extension must act as if it did not implement it. It MUST NOT advertise the capability, and it SHOULD reply with an INVALID_SYNTAX Notify payload if a client sends a modified request anyway.
sections.eli5: The host has to put up a sign saying "ID check only is fine here." Guests may only use that shortcut if they saw the sign.

sections.title: The Notification and the Modified Exchange
sections.content:
The CHILDLESS_IKEV2_SUPPORTED notification uses the ordinary Notify payload from RFC 5996. Its Protocol ID MUST be 1 because the message relates to an IKEv2 SA, its SPI Size MUST be zero, and its 2-octet message type MUST be 16418.

The modified IKE_AUTH exchange is shown in its EAP form; the non-EAP form is very similar. Compared with a normal exchange, the following are missing:

  • The optional notifications IPCOMP_SUPPORTED, USE_TRANSPORT_MODE, ESP_TFC_PADDING_NOT_SUPPORTED and NON_FIRST_FRAGMENTS_ALSO.
  • The SA payload.
  • The traffic selector payloads.
  • Any notification, extension payload or VendorID that has to do with Child SA negotiation.
sections.eli5: The special form is the normal one with the parts about setting up the chat torn out. Only the ID-checking parts stay.

sections.title: Security and IANA
sections.content:
The variation inherits all the security properties of regular IKEv2. The new notification cannot be forged or added by an adversary without detection, because the response to the initial exchange is authenticated by the AUTH payload of the IKE_AUTH exchange. Both peers also have to be configured to use the variation before the responder accepts a childless proposal.

IANA assigned the notify message type name CHILDLESS_IKEV2_SUPPORTED with the value 16418 in the "IKEv2 Notify Message Types" registry.
sections.eli5: The sign cannot be swapped by a sneaky person without getting caught, because the later ID check covers it.
